oil.summary: Crude posted its sharpest single-day rally in recent memory, with WTI surging 9.23% to $78.00/bbl and Brent jumping 9.43% to $83.18, as President Trump reimposed a blockade on Iran following a third consecutive weekend of U.S. strikes on Iranian targets. Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz lit the fuse, forcing traders to reprice supply-disruption risk across the complex. Heating oil led refined products higher (+4.73%), while RBOB lagged (-0.30%), suggesting the demand read is cautious even as supply fears dominate. On the supply side, Ukraine's reported strikes on all 10 of Russia's largest oil refineries—gutting up to 42% of domestic refining capacity—and attacks on 21 Russian shadow-fleet tankers in the Azov Sea add a second major supply overhang. Nigeria's output reaching a six-year high offers only partial offset.
drivers: Iran's Strait of Hormuz closure following Trump's reimposed blockade and a third weekend of U.S. airstrikes drove the headline spike in Brent and WTI
Ukraine's drone campaign has now struck all 10 of Russia's largest refineries, reportedly cutting up to 42% of Russian refining capacity, while 21 shadow-fleet tankers were hit in the Azov Sea
Nigeria's crude output hitting a six-year high in June provides incremental supply relief, but is insufficient to offset the Hormuz and Russia supply risk premium

gas.summary: The gas complex is deeply bifurcated today. TTF surged 5.63% to €51.395/MWh on the week's +16.46% move, almost certainly tracking the Hormuz closure and its implications for global LNG re-routing and Middle East supply risk. Henry Hub, by contrast, fell 1.29% to $2.902/MMBtu, extending a -10.57% weekly slide and suggesting ample domestic U.S. supply with limited spot demand pull. On the structural side, EU Russian LNG imports hit a record 9.97 million metric tons ahead of the 2027 ban—underscoring how dependent European buyers remain on Yamal LNG even as geopolitical pressure mounts. News flow on this sector is limited beyond these data points; the UAE's reported move to acquire a stake in a U.S. LNG export project adds a longer-term geopolitical dimension to Atlantic Basin LNG flows.
drivers: TTF's 5.63% single-day jump reflects Hormuz closure fears and re-routing risk for LNG tankers transiting the Persian Gulf
EU Russian LNG imports reached a record 9.97 million metric tons ahead of the 2027 ban, highlighting persistent European dependency on Yamal supply
Henry Hub continues to slide (-1.29% on the day, -10.57% on the week), reflecting domestic U.S. oversupply conditions decoupled from the European geopolitical premium

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs edged up 2.05% to $76.60, supported by the TTF spike feeding through to gas-fired generation costs, though the weekly EUA move remains slightly negative (-1.20%). France cut 6.4 GW of nuclear capacity on Monday as a heatwave raised river temperatures and constrained cooling water, tightening the continental power balance at a peak demand moment. Exelon's CEO publicly flagged U.S. blackout risk for 2027, citing inadequate supply additions against AI-driven load growth. On the cost curve, utility-scale solar rose 18% to a range of $40–$98/MWh due to tariffs, capital costs, and supply chain pressure, yet remains the cheapest unsubsidized generation source. Masdar secured $5.1 billion for the world's largest solar-and-battery project, and a separate report highlights geothermal beginning to undercut nuclear on cost.
drivers: France's 6.4 GW nuclear curtailment during a heatwave tightens European power supply and supports EUA prices alongside the TTF-driven gas generation cost increase
Exelon's CEO warned of U.S. blackouts in 2027 as AI-related load growth outpaces grid additions, reinforcing structural demand concerns for the power sector

Utility-scale solar LCOE rose 18% to $40–$98/MWh on tariff and capital cost pressures, while the Energy Institute's 2026 review confirmed global emissions hit another record high despite the clean energy build-out
